C0.quote: each voter may choose to cast her vote directly, or to delegate her vote
C0.note: Liquid democracy (delegable proxy voting): power index, delegation game equilibria, simulations.

C1.note: Theorem 1 axiomatic; Theorems 2-3 equilibrium; experiments are simulations. Power index results are the largest share.

C2.1.quote: d = (d1 , d2 , . . . , dn ) is called a delegation profile

C2.2.quote: delegation profiles can be usefully thought of as maps d : N → N ∪ {0}
C2.2.note: Input is a delegation (or direct binary vote); not a ranking, approval set, etc.

C2.3.quote: The agents’ ability to make the right choice
C2.3.note: Agents have accuracy qi and a held view of the correct state; accuracy is an attribute, not a submission.

C2.4.quote: agents want to vote truthfully in order to relay correct information
C2.4.note: Agents' accuracy-based truthful voting is assumed; rule applied to delegation profiles with no explicit statement on submission vs held attitude.

C3.1.quote: agents choose their delegations by aiming at maximizing the trade-off
C3.1.note: Delegation game analyses are strategic over delegations; the index analysis is not. Voters do not submit votes differing from a held attitude though; delegation is the strategic action. Coded SOME.

C3.2.loc: Preliminaries and Power Index sections, pp.5823-5826
C3.2.note: The index section does not state that voters submit held attitudes.

C5.1.quote: how the distribution of power in profiles is affected
C5.1.note: Power distribution (Gini) is not among the listed criteria; accuracy appears only inside utilities, with no welfare evaluation of rules.

VOT.quote_behav: our agents choose their delegations by aiming at maximizing the trade-off
VOT.note: Strategic in the delegation game; in the index analysis delegations are fixed. Information not specified.

C8.1.note: Iterated better response dynamics used in simulations.
